Engineering

Native C++ and Blueprint engineering standard

Use standard Unreal ownership/lifecycle conventions and narrow, explicit project contracts.

On this page
ScopeWorking sequenceAPI categoriesReview questions

Scope

All Source/RPG paths in asset pages are intended implementation paths, not files delivered here. Build scripts are documentation Python only. Project custom API signatures are design contracts; they are not compiled C++ or existing Blueprint nodes.

Prioritize one rule owner, explicit dependencies, descriptive names, shallow inheritance and testable transactions. Avoid parallel health/inventory/cooldown stacks, generic Manager/Utils containers and speculative service decomposition.

Working sequence

  1. Read the current phase, owner feature and individual asset contract before writing native types.
  2. Create native structs/enums/interfaces/schema bases needed now; compile with the installed Unreal Header Tool/build route.
  3. Add native implementation with explicit preconditions, errors, authority and asynchronous completion lifetime guards.
  4. Create Blueprint children and authored data; assign required references into actual consumers and test maps.
  5. Run native/data tests, Blueprint compile, multi-client fixture and rejection/regression cases. Record actual evidence separately from docs checks.
  6. Review API exposure, secret leakage, replication privacy, source IDs, cleanup and behavior after reconnect before moving on.

API categories

Engine API: known public types/functions with reference. PaperZD API: must be verified in installed release before exact signature is accepted. Project custom API: the names and contracts in this guide to implement. Backend endpoint proposal: HTTP service contract, never a magic Blueprint node. Pseudocode: illustrative ordering only. Every asset page uses these labels.

Review questions

Can a client change the fact directly? Does replay issue another reward? What owns this object after travel? Is its schema immutable? Does the Blueprint child duplicate native rules? Can a late async reply mutate a new character body? Is the success message sent after durable commit? Can missing art break physics? Answers must be visible in implementation and tests.

Evidence and external references

External links need internet; the manual itself remains offline. Public documentation does not prove installed compatibility.

  • Expose gameplay elements to Blueprints — Blueprintable, BlueprintType and property visibility concepts checked; project classes remain proposals.
  • Create an equippable native Actor example — Official 5.8 tutorial documents Tools > New C++ Class and Blueprint exposure. Its skeletal tool architecture is not copied into sprite presentation.

Planned game assets are not compiled assets. Values are proposals unless explicitly evidenced. Verification and limitations.
